title: Palindrome
prompt: Return True if word reads the same forwards and backwards, ignoring capitalization (so "Racecar" counts). Otherwise return False.
buggy_code:
def is_palindrome(word):
    # convert to lowercase so the check ignores capitalization
    backwards = word[::-1]
    return word == backwards

defects.note: The comment says the code lowercases the word, but nothing calls .lower(), so "Racecar" returns False. Flagging the comment or the comparison line both count.
[::-1] looks strange but is the standard, correct way to reverse a string in Python.

reference_solution:
def is_palindrome(word):
    # convert to lowercase so the check ignores capitalization
    word = word.lower()
    backwards = word[::-1]
    return word == backwards
